description: Notification plans (RFC 0003 §4.4): near-term reservation, at-time fill, the budget, equal-time ties, the horizon, ranges that start after or end before now, and coverage per alert kind with source gaps.

vectors.description: Proposal D7: five prayers, each with an at-time alert, a 10-minute before- and a 5-minute after-reminder; now at midnight; the default budget (60 requests, two near-term days, a 14-day horizon). The two near-term days reserve 30 requests and the other 30 go to the at-time alerts of the next six days: eight days of at-time alerts, two of reminders. Coverage ends at the third day's first reminder; at-time coverage runs to the ninth day's Fajr.
vectors.provenance: Proposal §7.5 ('30 near-term requests + 30 later at-time requests = eight days of at-time alerts and two days of reminders') and Appendix D7; RFC 0003 §4.4.

vectors.description: The same fixture with a budget of 20: the 30 near-term alerts don't fit, so the first 20 are kept in order and nothing later is selected. Coverage ends at the first omitted alert, 2 June's Dhuhr after-reminder; each kind's coverage ends at its own first omitted alert.
vectors.provenance: Proposal §7.5 rule 3 ('keep the earliest alerts up to the allowance … record the first omitted alert as the completeness cutoff'); RFC 0003 §4.4.

vectors.description: Maghrib's after-reminder and Isha's before-reminder both fire at 19:45, and the budget of two ends between them. Identity order keeps Maghrib's; Isha's is the first omitted alert, so coverage ends at 19:45 though an alert at 19:45 was selected.
vectors.provenance: Proposal §7.5 rule 3 ('Break equal-time ties by the canonical logical identifier'); RFC 0003 §4.2 Order, §4.4.

vectors.description: Edinburgh at 23:00 on 21 June, with a one-hour near-term window ending at midnight. The Isha before-reminder at 23:45 is near-term; Isha's alert at 00:15 is selected as a later at-time alert; its after-reminder at 00:30 is omitted. All three belong to 21 June.
vectors.provenance: RFC 0003 §4.2 (owning days), §4.4 (reservation, at-time fill).

vectors.description: A 14-day range with a 3-day horizon: nothing after the third day can be selected, so at-time coverage ends at the horizon, not at an omitted alert.
vectors.provenance: Proposal §7.5: the effective range is [now, min(candidateRange.end, now + horizon)); RFC 0003 §4.4.

vectors.description: A five-day near-term window with a one-day horizon: the window is clipped to the horizon, which ends coverage of every kind.
vectors.provenance: Proposal §7.5: 'A near-term window longer than the horizon cannot extend coverage or select requests beyond it.'

vectors.description: The range starts at noon, twelve hours after now: alerts from noon are selected, but nothing is known before noon, so every cutoff is now.
vectors.provenance: Proposal §7.5: 'if candidates begin later than now, the initial uncovered interval likewise makes coveredUntil == now'; RFC 0003 §4.4.

vectors.description: A range that ended before now: an empty effective range, no alerts, coverage at now.
vectors.provenance: Proposal §7.5: 'A candidate range ending at/before now produces an empty plan with coverage ending at now'.

vectors.description: A range that ends exactly at now is empty too.
vectors.provenance: Proposal §7.5; RFC 0003 §4.4.

vectors.description: 1 June's Isha is missing, but now is 06:00 on the 2nd, after every interval that gap makes: it doesn't shorten coverage. The range starts at midnight, as an in-process caller's would, and alerts before now aren't selected.
vectors.provenance: Proposal §7.5: 'a past-only gap does not shorten future coverage'; RFC 0003 §4.4.

vectors.description: At 01:00 on 2 June, 1 June's Isha may still be to come: every kind's interval contains now, so coverage is now.
vectors.provenance: Proposal §7.5: 'a gap containing now yields now'.

vectors.description: 3 June publishes no Isha; the budget holds everything. Before-reminder coverage ends at 18:00, an hour before the window opens at Maghrib; at-time coverage runs to 19:00 and after-reminder coverage to 19:20. Overall coverage is the earliest, 18:00.
vectors.provenance: Proposal §7.5: 'Each enabled kind's coverage uses its own offset transformation; at-time coverage is not shortened solely by a before-reminder's lookahead'; RFC 0003 §4.4.

vectors.description: The timetable ends on 3 June: every known alert fits, and coverage ends where the first unknown day's reminder could fall (Fajr's 30-minute reminder, 23:30 on the 3rd); at-time coverage ends at the 4th's midnight.
vectors.provenance: Proposal §7.5: 'A partial/expired timetable or a too-small budget shortens coverage without inventing missing alerts.'

vectors.description: A budget of zero selects nothing; each kind's coverage ends at its first alert.
A negative horizon counts as zero: the effective range is empty, so nothing is selected and every kind's coverage is now.
vectors.provenance: RFC 0003 §4.4: negative budget values count as zero.

vectors.description: A negative allowance with the default window and horizon selects nothing, like an allowance of zero: each kind's coverage ends at its first alert.
vectors.provenance: RFC 0003 §4.4: negative budget values count as zero.

vectors.description: A negative near-term window reserves nothing: the allowance goes to at-time alerts, and every reminder is left out, so reminder coverage ends at the first one.
vectors.provenance: RFC 0003 §4.4: negative budget values count as zero; the near-term window is [now, N).

vectors.description: Fajr only, with a reminder, over 14 days: the plan has room for all 28 alerts, yet after the two near-term days it selects at-time alerts only. Before-reminder coverage ends at the third day's reminder.
vectors.provenance: Proposal §7.5 rule 2: 'Later reminders stay in AlertSchedule for the in-process engine but are omitted from NotificationPlan.'

vectors.description: No prayer has settings: an empty plan whose coverage is the whole effective range, with no kind listed.
vectors.provenance: RFC 0003 §4.4: coveredUntil is the effective range's end when no kind is present.

vectors.description: Planning at 12:20 on 2 June: Dhuhr's alert (12:19) has passed and isn't selected, its after-reminder (12:24) is the first request, and the near-term window ends at 12:20 two days later.
vectors.provenance: RFC 0003 §4.4: only fire dates in [now, E) can be selected.
